goal: A streaming OSM PBF file reader that splits a file into blobs and inflates them on all cores, so every later build stage receives decoded primitive blocks without a C library.
scope: `src/build/pbf/file.zig`: read the BlobHeader / Blob framing (4-byte big-endian length, `OSMHeader` and `OSMData` types) using the protobuf wire codec from P1.07.
Support `raw`, `zlib_data` (std.compress.flate) and `lz4_data` (our LZ4) blobs; reject unsupported compression with a clear error.
Parse the HeaderBlock: bbox, required and optional features, `Sort.Type_then_ID`, replication timestamp.
A blob index pass (offset, size, kind) so workers can inflate blobs in parallel and hand them to consumers in file order.
Bounded memory: a fixed pool of inflate buffers reused across blobs, no per-blob heap allocation in steady state.
out_of_scope: Decoding nodes, ways and relations inside a PrimitiveBlock: P3.02.
notes: Zero external deps: Zig std and in-repo packages only.
Build throughput rule in docs/PLAN.md: report blobs per second and peak RSS.
docs/upstream/valhalla-perf-issues.md section 2e lists upstream parse timings to beat.
accept: Reads the upstream test extracts (utrecht, liechtenstein) and reports blob counts equal to an independent count from the oracle container.
Truncated and corrupt files return errors, never crash (unit tests with damaged fixtures).
Inflate throughput scales with thread count on a country extract (numbers recorded in the PR).
`zig build test` green.

goal: Decoders that turn a PrimitiveBlock into nodes, ways and relations with their tags, with no per-element allocation, so the tag transform and graph build can iterate OSM data at memory speed.
scope: `src/build/pbf/block.zig`: string table as slices into the inflated buffer; granularity, lat/lon offsets and date granularity.
DenseNodes: delta-decoded ids, lat, lon and the packed `keys_vals` stream; plain Node groups as well.
Ways: delta-coded refs, key/value index arrays. Relations: member ids (delta), roles, member types.
Iterator API: `nodes()`, `ways()`, `relations()` yielding views valid until the block is released; tags exposed as key/value string slices.
Coordinates converted to fixed-point 1e-7 degree `i32` exactly as OSM stores them.
Handle blocks with mixed groups and empty groups.
notes: Views borrow from the block buffer; document lifetimes in the API.
Fuzzing of this decoder is tracked in P3.38.
accept: Node, way and relation counts and a checksum over ids and tags match the oracle for the test extracts.
Round-trip test against PBFs written by the ASCII-map DSL from P1.18.
No allocator calls while iterating a block (counting allocator from P0.11).
`zig build test` green.

goal: An OSM XML reader producing the same node, way and relation views as the PBF path, so small hand-written fixtures and upstream XML test data can feed the build.
scope: `src/build/osmxml.zig` on top of `zig-xml`'s pull `Reader`: `<node>`, `<way>` with `<nd ref>`, `<relation>` with `<member>`, nested `<tag k v>`.
Entity decoding for tag values, negative ids, missing optional attributes.
Same iterator interface as the PBF block reader so build stages are input-agnostic.
Reject unsorted input with a clear error (the build expects nodes, then ways, then relations).
notes: Fixtures only: this path does not need to be fast.
`zig-xml` is a lenient tokenizer, so validate structure in our code.
accept: An XML fixture and the equivalent PBF produce identical element streams.
Malformed XML returns an error with a line number.
`zig build test` green.

goal: A node location store that resolves OSM node ids to coordinates without upstream's roughly 110 GiB way-node file and external sort, removing the largest IO cost of the build.
scope: `src/build/node_store.zig`: an id-indexed, delta-coded on-disk array of fixed-point coordinates, written sequentially as nodes arrive in id order.
Sparse block directory so lookups are one directory probe plus a short block decode; handle id gaps and unsorted input with a fallback path.
A usage bitset pass first (which node ids are referenced by routable ways) so only needed nodes are stored.
Parallel batched lookup API used by way processing, with read-ahead that follows way order.
Node use counts (1, 2, more) in a second bitset pair for intersection detection.
notes: docs/upstream/valhalla-perf-issues.md: #6312 and #4548 describe the upstream intermediates this replaces.
Build throughput rule: sequential, compact intermediates; report bytes per stored node.
accept: Every way node in the test extracts resolves to the same coordinate as the raw PBF.
Store size and lookups per second reported for a country extract; store is at most 6 bytes per kept node on average.
Peak RSS independent of extract size (measured on two extract sizes).
`zig build test` green.

goal: The framework that replaces Valhalla's Lua tag transform: comptime perfect-hash tag tables and the attribute model each way and node is reduced to, running on every core.
scope: `src/build/tags/table.zig`: comptime-generated perfect hash from tag key and value strings to enum ids, with a fallback for free-form values.
`WayAttrs` and `NodeAttrs` structs mirroring the fields upstream's `OSMWay` / `OSMNode` carry (class, use, access masks, speeds, surface, flags, name refs).
A `transformWay(tags) -> ?WayAttrs` / `transformNode(tags) -> ?NodeAttrs` entry point with the same keep-or-drop decision as `ways_proc` / `nodes_proc`.
Shared helpers ported from graph.lua: boolean normalisation, unit parsing hooks, default tables by highway type.
A per-thread scratch so transforms allocate nothing.
out_of_scope: The rule families themselves: P3.06 to P3.09.
Truck, HOV, toll and motorcycle tags: P5.03.
notes: No Lua and no script engine: this is plain Zig, so it is not capped at 8 states like upstream.
Keep the mapping to graph.lua line ranges in comments so goldens (P3.10) can be traced back.
accept: Unit tests for the hash tables (no collisions, unknown values fall through).
A way with no routable tags is dropped exactly when graph.lua drops it (cases enumerated in tests).
`zig build test` green.

goal: Highway classification ported from graph.lua: road class, use, surface, link and service-road attributes for every way, the base every costing model reads.
scope: `src/build/tags/highway.zig`: `highway=*` to road class (motorway to service_other) and `Use` (road, ramp, track, footway, path, steps, cycleway, living_street, driveway, alley, parking_aisle, ferry and the rest of upstream's enum).
Links (`*_link`), `service=*`, `junction=roundabout`, `tunnel`, `bridge`, `route=ferry` and `route=shuttle_train`.
Surface from `surface`, `tracktype` and defaults per class, to upstream's surface enum.
Internal-intersection, turn-channel candidates and `private` / `destination` flags that graph.lua sets at this stage.
Constants for every enum in `src/graph/constants.zig` with the same numeric values as upstream.
out_of_scope: Link reclassification after graph build: P5.02.
notes: Port rule by rule; do not reinterpret OSM tagging.
docs/upstream/valhalla-architecture.md section 5 describes the Lua stage.
accept: Table-driven tests covering every `highway` value graph.lua handles.
Feeds the golden comparison in P3.10 with zero diffs for these fields on the test extracts.
`zig build test` green.

goal: Access rules ported from graph.lua: per-mode forward and reverse access, oneway handling, and barrier or node access, so costing can decide who may use an edge.
scope: `src/build/tags/access.zig`: access masks for auto, truck, bus, taxi, motorcycle, moped, bicycle, pedestrian, wheelchair, HOV and emergency, forward and backward.
The access tag hierarchy (`access`, `vehicle`, `motor_vehicle`, mode-specific keys) with upstream's precedence, including `private`, `destination`, `delivery`, `permissive`, `no`.
`oneway`, `oneway:bicycle`, `cycleway=opposite*`, `junction` implied oneway, reversible lanes as upstream treats them.
Node access from `barrier=*`, `bollard`, `gate`, `access` on nodes, plus node type (gate, bollard, toll booth, border control).
16-bit access masks in our format; keep upstream's bit order in the low 12 bits.
notes: Access is correctness-critical: every rule gets a test named after its graph.lua section.
accept: Tests for each access key and value combination graph.lua handles, forward and reverse.
Zero diffs for access fields in the P3.10 goldens on the test extracts.
`zig build test` green.

goal: Speed, lane and naming attributes ported from graph.lua and the parser: parsed speed limits, default speeds, lane counts, names, refs and destination tags.
scope: `src/build/tags/speed.zig`: `maxspeed` parsing (kph, mph, `walk`, `none`, country zone codes), `maxspeed:forward` / `backward`, `maxspeed:hgv`, advisory speeds, and default speed by class and use.
Lanes: `lanes`, `lanes:forward`, `lanes:backward`, and raw `turn:lanes` strings carried for P6.03.
Names: `name`, `alt_name`, `official_name`, `name:<lang>`, `ref`, `int_ref`, tunnel and bridge names into a build-time string table.
Destination tags (`destination`, `destination:ref`, `destination:street`, `junction:ref`) carried for sign building in P6.02.
Speed type (tagged or classified) as upstream records it.
out_of_scope: Building signs and turn-lane records: P6.02 and P6.03.
notes: Speed parsing is hand-written; use `zig-regex` only if it is clearer than a small parser.
accept: Tests for each maxspeed format, including invalid input.
Zero diffs for speed, lane and name fields in the P3.10 goldens.
`zig build test` green.

goal: The bicycle and pedestrian tag rules our production traffic depends on: cycleways, bike networks, hiking difficulty, sidewalks, steps and related flags.
scope: `src/build/tags/bike_foot.zig`: `cycleway`, `cycleway:left/right/both`, `bicycle=use_sidepath`, `dismount`, cycle lane type (none, shared, dedicated, separated).
Bike networks from way tags (`lcn`, `rcn`, `ncn`, `icn`, `mtb`) with relation-derived networks left as a hook for the relations pass.
`sac_scale` to upstream's enum (hiking through difficult alpine hiking), `trail_visibility`, `mtb:scale`.
`sidewalk` left/right/both/no, `foot=*` designations, `footway=sidewalk|crossing`, `highway=steps`, `step_count`, `lit`, `wheelchair`, `indoor`, `elevator`.
Pedestrian type inputs (blind, wheelchair) that pedestrian costing reads.
out_of_scope: Pedestrian areas (plazas) and their traversal edges: later phase.
notes: These fields decide `max_hiking_difficulty`, `walkway_factor`, `use_tracks` and `use_roads` behaviour in P3.27 and P3.28.
accept: Tests for every `sac_scale`, `cycleway` and `sidewalk` value.
Zero diffs for these fields in the P3.10 goldens.
`zig build test` green.

goal: A golden test that proves our Zig tag transform equals upstream's graph.lua on real data, so tag parity is measured rather than assumed.
scope: A script in the oracle container that runs upstream `ways_proc` / `nodes_proc` under LuaJIT over every way and node of the test extracts and dumps the resulting attribute tables as line-delimited records.
`zr tags dump` producing the same record format from our transform.
A comparator that reports per-field diff counts and the first N differing OSM ids per field.
Goldens checked in (compressed) for the small upstream extracts; a larger country run available on demand.
A documented allow-list for deliberate differences, each with a reason.
out_of_scope: Post-build attributes (enhance stage): P3.19 and P5.01.
notes: LuaJIT runs only inside the dev-time oracle container; it is never a dependency of the product.
accept: Zero unexplained diffs on the upstream test extracts for all fields from P3.06 to P3.09.
The comparison runs in CI against the checked-in goldens.
`zig build test` green.

goal: Turn ways into graph edges: find intersections, split ways there, capture shapes, and handle loops and duplicates the way upstream's graph builder does.
scope: `src/build/edges.zig`: a node is a graph node when it is a way end, is used by more than one routable way, or carries routing-relevant node attributes.
Split each way into edges between graph nodes, keeping the intermediate coordinates as the edge shape and computing length from the shape.
Loop edges (same start and end) and ways that pass through a node twice: split as upstream does so no edge starts and ends at the same node.
Duplicate and zero-length edges, ways with fewer than two resolvable nodes: counted and reported, not fatal.
Emit a compact edge stream (way attrs ref, node ids, shape offset) consumed by graph assembly.
Runs in parallel over way chunks with deterministic output order.
out_of_scope: CSR assembly and opposing edges: P3.15.
notes: Determinism matters for P4.20: sort by a stable key, never by thread arrival order.
accept: Edge and node counts match the oracle's level-2 tile totals for the test extracts within the documented allow-list.
ASCII-map tests (P1.18) for loops, duplicated nodes and dead ends.
`zig build test` green.

goal: Graph format v1 defined in code: section file headers, the on-disk extern structs and a writer, with layout guaranteed at comptime.
scope: `src/graph/format.zig`: 64-byte section header (magic, format version, 16-byte dataset UUID, section kind, record size, count, xxh3 of payload) and the section kind enum.
`EdgeHot` (16 B) and `NodeHot` (8 B) exactly as in docs/PLAN.md, `first_edge: u32` CSR array, turn entry `u8`, opaque `NodeId` / `EdgeId` as `enum(u32)`.
Comptime assertions: `@sizeOf`, `@offsetOf`, little-endian target, `packed struct(u32)` members only inside `extern struct`.
`BundleWriter`: one file per section, 64 KiB alignment, payload hash, atomic rename of the bundle directory on success.
xxh3 implemented in-repo if std does not provide the needed variant.
notes: Never use a bare `packed struct` wider than 64 bits or as an array element.
docs/design/engine-and-format.md Q2 is the reference; upstream headers are listed only for attribute coverage.
accept: Layout assertions compile on x86-64 and aarch64.
Write then hex-compare a tiny bundle against a checked-in golden.
`zig build test` green.

goal: A graph reader that maps a bundle in well under a second, validates it, and exposes typed slices, plus `zr inspect` to look inside one.
scope: `src/graph/reader.zig`: mmap each section through the IO shim, check magic, version, record size, count and matching dataset UUIDs; one `@alignCast` per section boundary.
Typed accessors: `edge(id)`, `node(id)`, `outEdges(node)`, `oppEdge(edge)` computed as `first_edge[head] + opp_local`, `turnRow(node, in_local)`.
Clear errors for version mismatch, truncated files and mixed bundles.
`zr inspect <bundle>`: section table, counts, sizes, `--verify` to check payload hashes, `--edge` / `--node` to print one record.
The reader is immutable and shared by all threads; no per-thread caches.
notes: Startup checks headers only; hashing is offline (`--verify`).
docs/upstream/valhalla-perf-issues.md: #3953 and #3117 for the startup problem being solved.
accept: Open time under 50 ms for a country bundle on a warm page cache (measured in a test).
Corrupt or truncated sections are rejected with a specific error.
`zr inspect --verify` passes on a freshly built bundle.
`zig build test` green.

goal: The edge class table: every distinct combination of categorical edge attributes stored once and referenced by a 20-bit class id, so costing reduces to one table lookup per edge.
scope: `src/graph/class_table.zig`: `EdgeClass` tuple (use, road class, surface, forward and reverse access masks, toll, tunnel, bridge, roundabout, link, internal, destination-only, sac_scale, lit, sidewalk left/right, cycle lane, bike network, dismount, use_sidepath, HOV, truck route, restriction start/end flags).
Build-time interning with a hash map, deterministic id assignment (sorted by tuple bytes).
On-disk section and reader accessor `class(id)`.
Report distinct class counts; fail the build clearly if the 20-bit limit is exceeded.
Document which upstream DirectedEdge fields live in the class, in `EdgeHot`, or in cold data.
out_of_scope: Per-request factor tables indexed by class id: P3.25.
notes: Attributes read in the relax loop must be reachable from `EdgeHot` or the class table, never from cold data.
accept: Every costing-relevant DirectedEdge field from upstream is mapped (checklist in the PR).
Distinct class count for a country extract reported and far below 2^20.
`zig build test` green.

goal: Graph assembly: the edge stream becomes the hot topology sections, with opposing edges, local edge indices and node attributes in place.
scope: `src/build/assemble.zig`: create both directed edges per way segment, sort by start node, write `first_edge` (CSR) and `EdgeHot`.
`local` and `opp_local` indices (5 bits, up to 32 edges per node); nodes with more edges are split with zero-length connectors, counted in stats.
`len_m`, the four speed bytes, `class_id` from P3.14, `cold_checks` and `pred_speed` flags.
`NodeHot.attr`: access mask, node type, density placeholder, signal flag; node coordinates as a separate warm `2 x i32` array.
Validation pass: every edge has a correct opposing edge, lengths are non-zero, ids are dense.
Parallel by node-range chunk, deterministic output.
out_of_scope: Final node order: P3.21 and P4.02.
notes: Opposing edge is computed, not stored: this lifts upstream's 7-bit opposing index limit.
accept: Round trip: build an ASCII-map fixture, read it with P3.13, and check adjacency and opposing edges.
Validation pass reports zero errors on the test extracts.
Edges per second and peak RSS reported for a country extract.
`zig build test` green.

goal: Per-node turn tables holding what costing needs about each (incoming edge, outgoing edge) pair, deduplicated globally so they cost under a byte per node.
scope: `src/build/turns.zig`: for each node a `degree x degree` matrix of `u8` entries: `turn_type:3 | stop_impact:3 | name_consistent:1 | restricted:1`.
Turn type from the heading difference of the two edges at the node, using upstream's turn-degree thresholds.
Initial stop impact from the classes of the edges meeting at the node as upstream computes it; name consistency from shared names.
Global dedup of identical matrices into one pool; `NodeHot.turn_off` points into it.
Reader accessor `turnRow(node, in_local) []const u8`.
notes: Lookup is `pool[turn_off + in_local * degree + out_local]`; the edge-expanded graph is never materialised.
accept: Turn types match the oracle's `turntype` for sampled intersections (via P3.34 when available, hand-checked fixtures before).
Pool size reported; under 1 byte per node on a country extract.
`zig build test` green.

goal: Cold data sections: way ids, shapes and names stored compactly and out of the relax loop's way, read only by leg building, serializers and inspection.
scope: `src/graph/cold.zig`: one record per undirected edge reached through `cold_idx: u32` per directed edge.
Record: `u64` way id, shape as delta zigzag varints at 1e-7 degrees with a `u32` length, name references, mean elevation slot, speed limit.
A deduplicated string table for names (up to 255 names per edge).
Chunking by contiguous id range with a chunk directory, so pages stay local under any node order.
Accessors: `shape(edge, arena)` decoding in travel direction, `names(edge)`, `wayId(edge)`.
out_of_scope: Turn lanes and lane connectivity: P6.03.
notes: Lifts upstream limits: 15 names per edge, 65,535-byte shapes, 25-bit edgeinfo offset (docs/upstream/valhalla-perf-issues.md, #6148).
accept: Shapes round-trip exactly at 1e-7 degrees; reverse-direction decode tested.
Bytes per edge for cold data reported on a country extract.
`zig build test` green.

goal: Elevation stamped onto edges at build time: weighted grade, maximum up and down slopes and mean elevation, which bicycle and pedestrian costing use for hills.
scope: `src/build/elevation.zig`: sample each edge shape at upstream's posting interval using the sampler from P2.02.
Compute weighted grade (the 4-bit value, default 6 meaning flat), max up slope and max down slope with upstream's formulas and clamps.
Store `grade` in `EdgeHot.geom`, slopes and mean elevation in cold or side data as costing requires.
Skip gracefully when DEM tiles are missing; record coverage in build stats.
Parallel by edge chunk, sorted by DEM tile to keep tile cache hits high.
out_of_scope: Per-shape-point elevation in responses: later serializer work.
notes: `use_hills` and grade-based speed factors depend on this matching upstream.
accept: Weighted grade matches the oracle for sampled edges on a hilly test extract (via P3.34 or the oracle's `/locate`).
A build without DEM produces flat grades and a clear stat line.
`zig build test` green.

goal: The subset of upstream's enhance stage that pedestrian and bicycle routing needs: density, intersection types, dead ends and not-thru regions.
scope: `src/build/enhance.zig`: node and edge density (the 4-bit relative road density) with upstream's radius and scaling.
Intersection type per node (regular, false, dead end, fork) and the dead-end edge flag.
Not-thru region detection (bounded expansion from an edge that cannot reach a higher-class road) with upstream's limits.
Driving side per node defaulted, with a hook for admin data in P5.05.
Parallel, deterministic, writing back into the hot sections or class ids.
out_of_scope: Speed assignment, turn-type refinement and stop impact: P5.01.
notes: Density feeds pedestrian and bicycle cost factors, so it must match before P3.35 can pass.
accept: Density and dead-end flags match the oracle on sampled nodes and edges of a test extract.
ASCII-map tests for not-thru detection and dead ends.
`zig build test` green.

goal: One spatial index for snapping, map matching and `/locate`: a fine fixed grid with compact edge lists, replacing upstream's coarse bins and the duplicate map-matching grid.
scope: `src/graph/spatial.zig`: cells of 1/256 degree; a sorted directory of non-empty cell ids with offsets.
Each cell lists the undirected edges whose shape intersects it, as delta-varint ids.
Build: rasterise each shape through the grid (grid traversal from P1.04), parallel, deterministic.
Query API: cells within a radius of a point in expanding rings, and cells along a segment.
Section written through `BundleWriter`, read through the graph reader.
notes: docs/upstream/valhalla-perf-issues.md: #2529 explains why the bins are too coarse upstream.
accept: Every edge is found from any point on its shape (property test).
Index size reported; at most 3 bytes per edge on a country extract.
Ring queries return cells in non-decreasing distance order.
`zig build test` green.

goal: A node ordering interface with a Hilbert-curve order as the first implementation, so ids are spatially local now and the nested-dissection order can replace it later without touching other stages.
scope: `src/build/order.zig`: `Ordering` interface returning a permutation of provisional node ids.
Hilbert order over node coordinates using the curve from P1.04.
Apply the permutation: renumber nodes, re-sort edges, rewrite `head` values and every section keyed by node or edge id.
Record the ordering kind and a hash of the order in the bundle metadata.
out_of_scope: Nested dissection and making it the id order: P4.01 and P4.02.
notes: Upstream measured the locality gain from spatial ordering in PRs #4455 and #6342 (docs/upstream/valhalla-perf-issues.md).
accept: Graph is isomorphic before and after reordering (routes on a fixture are identical).
Median id distance between adjacent nodes reported before and after.
`zig build test` green.

goal: `zr build`: one command that runs every build stage from an OSM file to a bundle, restartable from any stage, with progress and stats.
scope: `src/build/driver.zig`: ordered stages (read, tags, node store, edges, assemble, turns, cold, elevation, enhance, order, spatial, validate, finalize).
`--from <stage>` and `--to <stage>` using intermediates in a work directory, like upstream's `start_stage` / `end_stage`.
Per-stage timing, rows per second, peak RSS and output sizes printed and written to `build-stats.json`.
Config: input files, DEM directory, work directory, thread count, output bundle path.
Fail fast with a clear message on missing inputs; clean up partial bundles.
out_of_scope: Determinism guarantees across thread counts: P4.20.
notes: Used by the ASCII-map test DSL, so it must also run fully in memory or a temp directory for tiny inputs.
accept: Builds the upstream test extracts end to end; `zr inspect --verify` passes.
Restarting from a middle stage produces a byte-identical bundle.
`zig build test` green.

goal: Location snapping: from a request location to ranked edge candidates with the same PathLocation semantics as Valhalla, on the new spatial index.
scope: `src/snap/search.zig`: ring search over the grid from P3.20, projecting the point onto candidate shapes with SIMD batches.

Location options with upstream names and defaults: `radius`, `heading`, `heading_tolerance`, `node_snap_tolerance`, `search_cutoff`, `street_side_tolerance`, `street_side_max_distance`, `preferred_side`, `rank_candidates`, `search_filter`.
Costing-aware filtering: an edge is a candidate only if the request's compiled costing allows it.
Result: correlated edges with percent along, projected point, distance, side of street, and snapping to nodes within tolerance (all edges at the node).
Ranking and tie-breaking as upstream so the same candidate wins.
notes: All scratch memory from the request arena.
This index is shared with map matching later; keep the query API general.
accept: Port the applicable cases from upstream's loki search tests.
Same top candidate as the oracle's `/locate` for at least 99% of a sampled location corpus.
Median snap time recorded in the bench results.
`zig build test` green.

goal: Reachability and connectivity checks for snapped locations, with the same error codes as Valhalla when no suitable edge exists.
scope: `src/snap/reach.zig`: bounded expansion from a candidate, forward and reverse, to count reachable nodes up to `minimum_reachability`.
Demote or drop candidates that fail reachability, as upstream does.
Connectivity: precomputed connected-component ids per node (build stage addition) so unconnected location pairs fail fast.
Error paths: no suitable edges near location (171), locations in unconnected regions (170), and the related loki errors with upstream messages.
Reuse the request arena and paged status arrays; no hashing.
out_of_scope: Service limit errors such as max distance (154): P3.33.
notes: docs/upstream/valhalla-perf-issues.md: PR #5384 shows Reach was a measurable hot spot upstream.
accept: Port upstream's reach test cases onto ASCII maps.
Island and one-way dead-end fixtures return the expected error codes.
`zig build test` green.

goal: The compiled costing framework: request options become a small table-driven POD that monomorphised kernels read with no virtual calls, under an explicit admissibility contract.
scope: `src/costing/compiled.zig`: `Compiled` POD with a class-id to factor table (`+inf` means not allowed), speed to seconds-per-metre table, turn-class to cost table, and scalars.
Kernel interface used by `Search(K, Q)`: `edgeCost`, `turnCost`, `slowAllowed` (noinline cold path), `unitSize`, plus `edgeLowerBound` and `turnLowerBound`.

Contract documented and asserted: I1 edge bound never exceeds real cost, I2 turn bound never exceeds real transition cost, I3 costs non-negative and forbidden is infinite, I4 features are monotone or supply a scalar floor, I5 bounds round down.
128-bit metric key hashing the static projection of the POD.
A compile cache keyed by the canonicalised options; compile cost budget about 100 microseconds.
`Cost { cost: f32, secs: f32 }` matching upstream arithmetic.
out_of_scope: Option parsing shared across models: P3.26.
Metric customisation from the POD: P4.04.
notes: docs/design/engine-and-format.md Q1 defines the invariants.
Three or four kernels, not one per model: models differ in tables more than code.
accept: A toy kernel passes a property test of I1 to I3 over random options.
Equal compiled tables from different raw options produce the same metric key.
No allocation after the compile cache is warm.
`zig build test` green.

goal: The shared costing base ported from DynamicCost: common option parsing with upstream names, ranges and defaults, and the penalties every model shares.
scope: `src/costing/base.zig`: port `ParseBaseCostOptions` (maneuver, gate, private access, destination-only, toll booth, ferry, rail ferry, country crossing, service, closure and similar penalties and costs, `use_*` factors, `shortest`, `ignore_*` flags).
Range clamping and defaults identical to upstream's ranged-default handling.
Shared transition-cost pieces: turn-type costs, stop impact, name consistency, density factors.
Shared allowed checks: access mask, closures hook, destination-only and private access handling.
Each option contributes its lower-bound effect for the admissibility contract.
out_of_scope: Model-specific formulas: P3.27, P3.28 and Phase 5.
Time and traffic dependent parts: P5.14 and P10.05.
notes: Costs stay `f32` so per-call parity (gate A) can reach 1e-5.
accept: Table tests: every base option name, default, minimum and maximum equals upstream.
Out-of-range values clamp or reset exactly as upstream.
`zig build test` green.

goal: Pedestrian costing ported in full from pedestriancost.cc, including every option the consuming apps send, with per-call cost parity against Valhalla.
scope: `src/costing/pedestrian.zig`: `Allowed`, `EdgeCost`, `TransitionCost` and their reverse forms compiled into the POD and kernel.

Options with upstream defaults and ranges: `walking_speed`, `walkway_factor`, `sidewalk_factor`, `alley_factor`, `driveway_factor`, `step_penalty`, `elevator_penalty`, `max_hiking_difficulty`, `use_tracks`, `use_living_streets`, `use_ferry`, `use_hills`, `use_lit`, `service_penalty`, `service_factor`, `max_distance`, `type` (foot, wheelchair, blind) and transit-related distances.
Grade-based speed factors, surface and sac_scale access limits, steps and elevator handling.
Lower bounds per the admissibility contract, including factors below 1.
Unit size and the A* cost factor equivalent for the L2 heuristic.
out_of_scope: Multimodal and transit use of pedestrian costing: P9.04.
notes: Port formula by formula with a comment naming the upstream function.
Production requests use `walkway_factor`, `sidewalk_factor`, `use_tracks`, `use_living_streets`, `max_hiking_difficulty`, `step_penalty`.
accept: Gate A: per-call edge and transition cost within 1e-5 relative of the oracle (harness in P3.35).
Port the pedestrian cases from upstream's sif tests.
Property test of invariants I1 to I3 over the legal option ranges.
`zig build test` green.

goal: Bicycle costing ported in full from bicyclecost.cc with every option, with per-call cost parity against Valhalla.
scope: `src/costing/bicycle.zig`: `Allowed`, `EdgeCost`, `TransitionCost` and reverse forms compiled into the POD and kernel.

Options with upstream defaults and ranges: `bicycle_type` (road, hybrid, cross, mountain), `cycling_speed`, `use_roads`, `use_hills`, `avoid_bad_surfaces`, `use_ferry`, `use_living_streets`, `bss_return_cost`, `bss_return_penalty`, plus base penalties.
Road-class and cycle-lane factors, bike-network preference, surface limits per bicycle type, dismount and use_sidepath handling, grade-based speed and penalty tables.
Turn costs including the bicycle-specific stress terms.
Lower bounds per the admissibility contract.
out_of_scope: Bike share stations and mode changes: P9.07.
notes: Production requests use `use_roads` and `use_hills`.
Depends on grades from P3.18 and bike tags from P3.09.
accept: Gate A: per-call cost within 1e-5 relative of the oracle (harness in P3.35).
Port the bicycle cases from upstream's sif tests.
Property test of invariants I1 to I3 over the legal option ranges.
`zig build test` green.

goal: The search core every endpoint will share: an exact label-setting A* over directed-edge labels, generic over costing kernel and queue, with zero steady-state allocation.
scope: `src/search/search.zig`: `Search(comptime K, comptime Q)` with the relax loop from docs/design/engine-and-format.md Q3.
32-byte label: `cost f32, secs f32, pred u32, edge u32, dist_m u32, tcost f32, flags u32, ctx u32`.
Edge status as a two-level paged array (directory by `id >> 12`, 16 KB pages from the request arena), reset by rewinding the arena.
4-ary heap of `{key u32, label u32}` with lazy deletion; a potential interface with the L2 implementation (haversine times fastest seconds per metre).
Forward and mirrored reverse expansion from one code path.
Cancellation: deadline and atomic flag checked every 1024 pops; no recursion anywhere.
out_of_scope: Origin and destination partial edges: P3.30.
notes: No hierarchy pruning and no shortcuts: results are exact.
Mark cold checks `noinline`; watch instantiation count.
accept: Matches a reference Dijkstra on random ASCII-map graphs (property test, cost equality).
No allocator calls on the second and later runs of the same search.
Throughput measured by P3.36.
`zig build test` green.

goal: Correct handling of where routes start and end: partial edges, several candidates per location, trivial routes and both ends on the same edge.
scope: `src/search/endpoints.zig`: seed the queue from every origin candidate with partial edge cost for the remaining fraction, in both travel directions where allowed.
Destination handling: partial cost to the projected point, all destination candidates, node-snapped destinations.
Trivial routes: origin and destination on the same edge in order, and the out-and-back case when they are in the wrong order.
Heading and side-of-street preferences applied as upstream applies them to candidate costs.
Result: an ordered list of (edge, begin fraction, end fraction) plus accumulated cost and time.
out_of_scope: Multiple locations and through or via handling: P3.31.
notes: This is where most small parity diffs come from; test against the oracle on short routes first.
accept: ASCII-map tests for same-edge, opposite-direction, node-snapped and multi-candidate cases.
Gate B holds on a corpus of routes under 2 km.
`zig build test` green.

goal: Routes through more than two locations with Valhalla's location types: break, through, via and break_through.
scope: `src/search/multi.zig`: leg-by-leg search between consecutive locations, carrying the arrival edge into the next leg.
`break` and `break_through` end a leg; `through` and `via` continue the same leg; `through` and `break_through` forbid u-turns at the location.
Carry elapsed time across legs for later time-dependent support.
Waiting and `date_time` hooks left as explicit TODO interfaces for P5.15.
notes: Leg boundaries must match upstream so `trip.legs[]` lines up for clients that stitch leg shapes.
accept: ASCII-map tests for each location type, including the no-u-turn rule.
Leg count and per-leg lengths equal the oracle on a multi-location corpus.
`zig build test` green.

goal: Turn a found path into legs: the stitched shape, and the length, time and cost summaries a route response needs.
scope: `src/search/legs.zig`: decode cold shapes in travel direction, trim partial first and last edges, drop duplicate joint points.
Length in metres and elapsed seconds per edge and per leg, recomputed by a recost pass so times match upstream's reporting.
Leg and trip summary fields: `length`, `time`, `cost`, bounding box, `has_toll`, `has_highway`, `has_ferry` and the other summary flags.
Output as plain structs in the request arena; no protobuf intermediates.
SIMD polyline encoding of the leg shape through P1.02.
out_of_scope: Maneuvers and the full trip-leg attribute set: P6.05.
notes: Keep this path cheap: for `directions_type: none` requests it is most of the post-search time.
accept: Shape equals the oracle's decoded leg shape point for point when paths match.
Summary length within 0.5% and time within 1% of the oracle.
`zig build test` green.

goal: The `/route` endpoint for `directions_type: none`, response-compatible with Valhalla, which is exactly what the consuming apps call today.
scope: `src/api/route.zig`: request parsing for `locations`, `costing`, `costing_options`, `directions_type`, `units`, `shape_format` (polyline6, polyline5, geojson), `id`, `language` passthrough.
Response: `trip.locations`, `trip.legs[].shape`, `trip.legs[].summary`, `trip.summary`, `status`, `status_message`, `units`, `language`, `id`.
Service limits per costing (`max_distance`, `max_locations`) with error 154 and friends, matching upstream messages and HTTP status.
Error JSON for no-path (442) and the loki errors from P3.24.
Per-phase timings (parse, snap, search, legs, serialize) in the access log.
out_of_scope: OSRM, GPX and pbf output: P6.14 and P6.15.
notes: Parity gate H applies: keys, types, enums and error codes are exact.
accept: Golden JSON key sets and types equal the oracle for the foot and bike corpus (gate H).
Error cases return the same `error_code` and HTTP status as the oracle.
`zig build test` green.

goal: A test-only importer that converts Valhalla graph tiles into our format, so both engines can route on the identical graph and algorithm differences are separated from builder differences.
scope: `src/cli/import_valhalla.zig`: read `.gph` files or a `tiles.tar` with `index.bin`; local level (2) only, ignoring shortcuts and transitions.
Mirror upstream bitfield layouts with `extern struct` plus `packed struct(u64)` words exactly as recorded in docs/upstream/valhalla-architecture.md section 3, including the header padding quirk.
Map DirectedEdge and NodeInfo fields into `EdgeHot`, the class table, turn tables and cold data; decode EdgeInfo shapes (7-digit) and names.
Resolve cross-tile end nodes into dense ids; rebuild opposing-edge local indices.
Write a normal bundle through `BundleWriter` so every other tool works on it.
out_of_scope: Any runtime use of Valhalla tiles.
Transit level and hierarchy levels 0 and 1.
notes: This never ships in the server binary path.
Tile version check: warn like upstream when the major version differs.
accept: Imports the oracle's tiles for a test extract; node and edge counts equal the tile header totals for level 2.
Sampled edges and nodes equal the oracle's `/locate` output field by field.
`zig build test` green.

goal: The costing parity harness for gate A: compare our edge and transition costs call by call with Valhalla's, so a wrong formula is caught before any route is compared.
scope: A small instrumented program built in the oracle container that links upstream and dumps `EdgeCost` and `TransitionCost` for sampled (predecessor edge, edge, options) tuples.
`zr parity costing`: evaluate the same tuples on a bundle imported with P3.34 and report relative error per call and per option set.
Option-set sampling across the legal ranges plus the exact production option sets.
Path-level check: recost oracle paths with our costing and compare to the oracle-reported cost (tolerance 1e-4).
Machine-readable report consumed by the phase gate.
notes: Gate A is a hard gate: any violation is a bug in the port, not noise.
accept: At least 10^7 sampled calls for pedestrian and bicycle within 1e-5 relative error.
Recost of oracle paths within 1e-4.
Any failing tuple is printed with enough detail to reproduce.
`zig build test` green.

goal: Experiment E1: measure how fast the search core settles labels on a real country graph, to confirm the data layout before more is built on it.
scope: Run plain edge-based Dijkstra (no potential) with the pedestrian kernel, and a stub motor kernel, on a Germany bundle from random sources to 10^6 settled labels.
Record nanoseconds per settled label, cache misses and branch misses per label (tooling from P0.12).
Measure the oracle's label throughput for the same expansions for comparison.
Write up results and any layout changes proposed in `docs/experiments/E1.md`.
notes: Pass line from docs/PLAN.md: at most 150 ns per settled label and at least 5x upstream label throughput.
If it fails, revisit the record layout before continuing.
accept: Results file committed with hardware, dataset and commit.
Pass or fail stated against the 150 ns and 5x lines, with the follow-up issue opened if it fails.
`zig build test` green.

goal: Tests that prove `/height` and `/route` allocate nothing from the heap once warm, locking in the per-request arena design.
scope: A test harness that warms each endpoint, then swaps in the counting allocator from P0.11 and replays a request mix.
Assert zero allocator calls outside the request arena for `/height` and `/route`.
Assert the arena high-water mark stays under the per-request cap for the corpus.
A helper so later endpoints add themselves with one line.
notes: docs/upstream/valhalla-perf-issues.md: #5172 is the heap ratchet this design avoids.
accept: Tests fail if a heap allocation is introduced on either endpoint's steady-state path.
Arena high-water figures recorded for the corpus.
`zig build test` green.

goal: Fuzz targets for the two parsers that read untrusted bytes in this phase: the OSM PBF reader and the graph bundle loader.
scope: `std.testing.fuzz` targets for blob framing, PrimitiveBlock decoding and DenseNodes.
Fuzz target for bundle header validation and section accessors on mutated bundles.
Seed corpora from the test extracts and a tiny bundle.
Every crash found becomes a regression test.
out_of_scope: Request parser and codec fuzzing: P1.20.
notes: A corrupt bundle must be rejected at open, never read out of bounds later.
accept: Each target runs for a fixed budget in CI without findings.
Bounds are checked on every offset read from a file (review checklist in the PR).
`zig build test` green.

goal: Upstream's behaviour spec for foot and bike routing running against our engine: the relevant gurka suites ported onto the ASCII-map DSL.
scope: Select the gurka test files that exercise pedestrian and bicycle access, costing options, hiking difficulty, steps, sidewalks, cycleways, one-ways for bikes, and basic route shape.
Port each as a Zig test using the DSL from P1.18 and `zr build` in a temp directory.
Port the assertion helpers needed: expected path by way names, expected failure with error code.
Keep a ledger file listing every upstream gurka test and its status (ported, deferred with the owning issue, not applicable).
out_of_scope: Access restriction and time-dependent suites: P5.20.
notes: Where our exact search finds a cheaper path than the upstream expectation, record it in the ledger with the recost evidence rather than editing the expectation silently.
accept: All selected suites pass or are explained in the ledger.
The ledger covers all 136 upstream gurka files.
`zig build test` green.

goal: The Phase 3 gate and experiment E8: prove parity and acceptable latency for pedestrian and bicycle routing before any production traffic is moved.
scope: Run gates A, B and C from docs/PLAN.md on the foot and bike corpus and on 100k random routes: same graph via P3.34, oracle with hierarchy pruning disabled for gate C.
Run the default-oracle comparison and classify every differing route by cause (cheaper for us, tie, snap difference, bug).
Latency: p50 and p99 for the production-shaped corpus against the Phase 0 baseline.
Write `docs/gates/P3.md` with numbers, hardware, data and commit.
notes: Gate B is absolute: our cost of our path must never exceed our cost of the oracle's path.
accept: Gate A within 1e-5 per call and 1e-4 per path; gate B at 100%; gate C within 1e-4 on at least 99.9%.
Length and time within 1% of the oracle where paths match.
p50 and p99 no worse than the baseline.
Report committed.

goal: zig-routing serving `/route` beside Valhalla on the production routing box with the full regional bundle, receiving mirrored traffic, with memory verified.
scope: Build the production region bundle and copy it to the box.
Extend the service unit from P2.07 to serve `/route`; keep it private to the same clients as the existing service.
Mirror a sample of live `/route` requests and diff responses with `zr diff`; collect a day of results.
Record RSS, page-cache use and latency under the mirrored load.
Document rollback (stop the unit; clients are unaffected because they still use Valhalla).
out_of_scope: Changing which server the apps call: P3.42.
notes: Needs maintainer access to the box; no secrets or addresses belong in the repository or this issue.
accept: Maintainer approves the deployment and provides access.
One day of mirrored traffic with no gate B violations and no errors that Valhalla did not also return.
RSS within the memory budget in docs/PLAN.md with headroom recorded.
Results summarised in `docs/gates/P3-shadow.md`.

goal: The consuming apps route through zig-routing first, with Valhalla kept as the automatic fallback during a soak period.
scope: Switch the apps' primary routing URL to zig-routing and set the existing Valhalla service as the fallback.
Watch error rates, fallback rate and latency for the soak period; alert on fallback spikes.
Keep `zr diff` sampling running through the soak.
Write down the rollback step (revert the URL) and who can perform it.
out_of_scope: Removing the fallback and decommissioning Valhalla: P13.01.
notes: The apps already try servers in order, so this is a configuration change, not a code change.
accept: Maintainer performs or approves the configuration change.

Outcome and numbers recorded in `docs/gates/P3-cutover.md`.
